# An instance added to a themed container keeps theme: null

## Context

`WorkstationNL › the header overflow action opens a body-mounted menu with live Workstation skin` (`test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNL.spec.mjs:2688`) is one of the three unowned `WorkstationNL` reds on #17844. It fails at `dev@cce07cdade` and `dev@3044d7f86b` on its first theme assertion: the overflow control's `theme` is `null`, not `neo-theme-neo-dark`.

A Neural Link read of the control's parent chain on `dev@3044d7f86b` (dark boot) shows where the theme config stops:

| component | className | `theme` |
|---|---|---|
| `neo-button-38` (the overflow control) | `Neo.button.Base` | `null` |
| `neo-tab-header-toolbar-4` | `Neo.tab.header.Toolbar` | `null` |
| `neo-tab-container-3` | `Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.TabContainer` | `null` |
| four layout containers | `Neo.container.Base` | `null` |
| `neo-dock-workspace-1` | `Workstation.view.Workspace` | `null` |
| `neo-viewport-1` | `Workstation.view.Viewport` | `neo-theme-neo-dark` |

`getTheme()` still resolves `neo-theme-neo-dark` at every level by walking up to the Viewport. The Viewport renders into the body, so today's paint is correct: a light-carried window (`?theme=neo-theme-neo-light`) paints its overflow menu light. What is missing is the config.

## The Problem

`component.Base#getTheme` documents the contract: "The inherited theme travels as a config (`container.Base#afterSetTheme` propagates it), and a child inside a themed scope carries no theme class of its own by design, so the theme config is the first thing to read at every level." Two of the three ways an item reaches a container honor it:

- **An item config** resolves at creation: its own theme, then `itemDefaults`, the class default, the container's (`createItem`'s object branch, #18105).
- **A live theme change** reaches every instance item (`container.Base#afterSetTheme`).
- **An instance added through `add()` / `insert()`** takes `createItem`'s `NeoInstance` branch, which runs `item.set(config)` and never reads `me.theme`. An instance created without a theme stays `null`, and every config item created beneath it inherits that `null`.

A unit probe on `dev@3044d7f86b` isolates the third path. Under a container with `theme: 'neo-theme-neo-dark'`:
- A `{module: Container, items: [{module: Component}]}` config reads `dark` for itself and its child.
- The same tree built with `Neo.create` and then `add()`ed reads `null` for both, while its child's `getTheme()` resolves `dark`.
- After `container.theme = 'neo-theme-neo-light'`, the adopted instance and its child both read `light`.

The gap is at adoption only.

The Workstation moved onto that path in #18375 (2026-09-05). The Viewport's `{module: Workspace}` item became `Neo.create(Workspace, …)` followed by `add(workspace)`, now in `ViewportController` (`:210`, `:243`) since #18596. The arm, added on 08-31 against the config path, is red in every title-keyed census since `22c183ccf9` (09-09).

Anything that reads the theme config under an adopted subtree is affected; the dock header's overflow control is the case the arm pins. In action mode (`tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs` `createActionControl`, through `toolbar.Base#addActionContribution`) the control inherits `null`. `button.Base` then hands that `null` to its body-mounted `menuList` (`button/Base.mjs:350`–`360`), which carries no theme class and paints whatever scope the body has. The floating mode sidesteps this by passing `theme: owner.getTheme()`.

## The Architectural Reality

- `container/Base.mjs` `createItem`: the object branch resolves `item.theme = item.theme || defaults.theme || module.config.theme || me.theme`; the `NeoInstance` branch has no theme rung.
- `grid.Container` passes `theme: me.theme` to each child it builds through `beforeSetInstance` (six sites). That is the per-site form of the same rung, for children a container constructs itself; an instance handed to `add()` has no such site.
- `component/Base.mjs` `afterSetTheme`: a theme equal to the physical parent's carries no class (`inheritsTheme`); any other stamps its class. An adopted in-tree instance inheriting through the parent rung therefore adds no class to its root, which is what the arm expects (`controlThemeClasses: []`).
- `main/addon/Stylesheet.mjs:80` puts `themes[0]` on the body as the window's default scope. Nested scopes are CSS-variable scopes on top of it, by design.

## The Fix

Recommended: give `createItem`'s `NeoInstance` branch the object branch's last rung, reading the instance's theme before the move re-parents it. An adopted instance takes the container's theme when it carries none, or when the theme it carries is the one it inherited, meaning it equals its previous container's theme. A theme of its own, one that differs from its previous container's, stays, just as an item config's own theme does.

The comparison with the previous container is what keeps moves correct. Live panes move between containers instead of being recreated. A rung that only filled an unset theme would pin the first container's theme on a moved pane, and its descendants would resolve that stale scope through `getTheme()` in the next container. That is worse than today, where the unset config walks up to the current scope.

Alternatives considered:
- **The Workstation adds its Workspace as a config, or passes the Viewport's theme.** This fixes one root and leaves the gap for every other app that adopts instances. #18461 is reshaping that composition anyway.
- **The overflow action control resolves `owner.getTheme()` at creation, like the floating mode.** This patches one consumer. It stamps a duplicate class on an in-tree control, which the arm rejects, and leaves every other theme-config reader under an adopted subtree as it is.
- **Filling only an unset theme (`item.theme ??= me.theme`).** It turns `:2688` green but pins the first container's theme on every instance that moves afterwards, as above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An instance created without a theme and added to a themed container reads the container's theme, and so does the subtree it built before. Red-first in `test/playwright/unit/container/ItemTheme.spec.mjs`.
- [ ] An instance that inherited its theme follows the container it moves into; an instance carrying its own theme keeps it, on adoption and on a move.
- [ ] An in-tree adopted root that inherits its theme carries no theme class, and a later container theme change still reaches adopted instances.
- [ ] `WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` run whole with `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` wired: the header overflow arm passes, and every other arm keeps its census result.
- [ ] The unit tier stays green.
- [ ] An explicit theme on a descendant of an adopted or moved subtree survives, and only the themes that were inherited retarget. *(Added 2026-09-14 on @neo-gpt's review of PR #18679: the first repair reached the live cascade, which assigned the new theme to every descendant, so an adopted subtree lost a child's explicit theme while the same tree built from configs kept it.)*

## Out of Scope

- An own theme that happens to equal its previous container's is indistinguishable from an inherited one, and follows the move. Telling them apart would need the config to record where its value came from.
- The overflow plugin's floating-mode theme wiring, which already resolves its scope.
